title: Inhaled Combined Budesonide-Formoterol as Needed in Mild Asthma
authors: O'Byrne PM, FitzGerald JM, Bateman ED, Barnes PJ, Zhong N, Keen C, et al.
population: Patients aged 12 years and older with mild asthma eligible for GINA step 2 treatment in 18 countries; twice-daily placebo plus terbutaline 0.5 mg as needed, twice-daily placebo plus budesonide 200 µg-formoterol 6 µg as needed, or twice-daily budesonide 200 µg plus terbutaline as needed, double blind
funder: Funded by AstraZeneca; the registry names AstraZeneca as lead sponsor and responsible party.
authorConflicts: Four of the ten authors were employees of AstraZeneca Research and Development (Gothenburg and Barcelona); three other authors (FitzGerald, Bateman, Reddel) were authors of the 2019 GINA statement.
result: 3836 patients were analysed (1277 terbutaline, 1277 budesonide-formoterol, 1282 budesonide maintenance). Weeks with well-controlled asthma: 34.4% with as-needed budesonide-formoterol against 31.1% with terbutaline (OR 1.14, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.30) and 44.4% with budesonide maintenance (OR 0.64, 0.57 to 0.73). Annual severe exacerbation rates were 0.20 with terbutaline, 0.07 with as-needed budesonide-formoterol and 0.09 with budesonide maintenance (rate ratio 0.36, 0.27 to 0.49, against terbutaline). Adherence to maintenance budesonide was 78.9%; median metered inhaled glucocorticoid dose with as-needed budesonide-formoterol was 57 µg/day, 17% of the 340 µg/day with maintenance.
